title: Demis Hassabis proposes a FINRA-style body to regulate frontier AI
summary: In a July 14 manifesto Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis called for a US-led, industry-funded AI standards body that could vet frontier models before release and even pause the industry.
body_markdown: [Demis Hassabis published a manifesto](https://x.com/demishassabis/article/2076957440109625718) on July 14 calling for an independent AI standards body modeled on FINRA. Hassabis runs Google DeepMind and shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold. Frontier labs would share models with the body up to 30 days before release, tested for cyber, bio, and deception risks. [He told Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/14/demis-hassabis-ai-regulation-google-deepmind) he wants it US-led, industry-funded, and running before year-end. The body could later require models to pass before US deployment and even [coordinate a slowdown across the labs](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/14/deepmind-ceo-calls-for-an-independent-standards-body-to-regulate-frontier-ai/). Hassabis says AGI is probably only a few years away. Nadella and Altman back the idea.

title: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model
summary: Kimi K3 is the largest open-weight model so far, scores near Fable 5 on the Intelligence Index, and tops the blind-voted Frontend Code arena.
body_markdown: [Moonshot AI released Kimi K3](https://www.kimi.com/blog/kimi-k3) on July 16. It has 2.8 trillion parameters and is the largest open-weight model so far. On the blind-voted [Frontend Code arena](https://lmarena.ai/leaderboard) it is first at 1,679, ahead of Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. On the broader [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/) Intelligence Index it scores 57, just behind Fable 5 at 60 and Sol at 59. It is on kimi.com, subscription and API at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output. The weights open on July 27.
